assumptions: Robustness as defined by Wimsatt/Campbell implies epistemic reliability.
Bayesian updating can be parameterized by robustness metrics.
Independence of initial conditions serves as a proxy for evidence quality.
definition.falsification: If consensus formed from diverse initial conditions performs worse on unseen test sets than simple majority voting or isolated expert evidence, robustness is not a reliable heuristic.
definition.statement: An agent's reliance on group consensus is epistemically justified when the individual contributions demonstrate robustness—invariant consistency across diverse initial conditions—rather than convergence to a specific prior.
definition.uncertainty: The mapping between theoretical robustness and computational consensus reliability is hypothesized but unmeasured.
